title: The show "How Come" with Eddie Hunter and Sidney Bechet
summary: The Eddie Hunter show "How Come", dated by Albertson to the early twenties, with Bessie Smith briefly in it and Bechet playing a Chinese man; Hunter's first stage show.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So then, after that opening night I had nothing to do but keep going. I sailed, you know. And from that -- that was the show, "How Come."
The Eddie Hunter Show.
Eddie Hunter Show, "How Come." See --
That was what year, now, "How Come"?
I believe that was in '34.
No, that had to have been --
Before that?
Oh, sure, because that was the show Bessie had been in briefly.
Yes. And they couldn't do anything with her.
Yes. This would have had to have been very early twenties.
Well, that was it. Anyhow --
I have all that. I have all the
dates on that, on the "How Come". But that was -- you were talking about when you first came to New York.
Yeah. Well, anyhow --
Around the time when you made these records for Black Swan.
Yeah.
Then when you did "How Come", it must have been around the same time. Sidney Bechet was in that.
Yes, Sidney Bechet.
And he played "How Come".
He did?
He was -- about a Chinese man, right, "How Come"?
Yeah, oh, sure, Bechet was. Yes, made up as a Chinaman.
And that was at the Apollo on 42nd Street.
42nd Street. We're the first group down there, you know, on Broadway. We called it 42nd and Broadway, you see.
That was the first stage show you did.
First stage show, yes.
What did you do in that?
Oh, let me see. Yeah, the first -- I
(Inaudible).
Uh-huh. Did I do anything in that show? I don't remember. I have to think way back.
